terms.meaning: The part of the Earth where life exists: the fourth part of the Earth, with all its living things.
The study of how living things interact with their physical, chemical and biological surroundings.
The natural balance among the organisms living together.
A community of plants and animals together with their surroundings, including the non-living part.
The surroundings of an organism, natural (geographical) or cultural (man-made).
A substance that causes pollution, visible like smoke or invisible like bacteria.
The variety of plants (flora) and animals (fauna) in a region.

items.name: Causes of environmental pollution
items.formula: Over-population, industries, cities, over-use of resources and vehicles.
items.example: Man-made pollutants are more harmful than natural ones.

items.name: Air pollution
items.formula: Pollutants: CO2, CO, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, CFCs. Effects: ozone loss, global warming, breathing problems.
items.example: Control: fewer vehicle emissions, more trees, clean energy.

items.name: Water pollution
items.formula: Sources: industrial effluents, sewage, farm waste, oil spills. Effects: cholera, typhoid, jaundice, death of water life.

items.name: Soil pollution
items.formula: From industrial, mining, urban and farm waste; it lowers fertility and kills soil organisms.
items.example: Control: careful use of fertilizers and pesticides.

items.name: Noise pollution
items.formula: Unwanted sound from industry, vehicles and aircraft; it causes hearing loss, headaches and heart disease.
items.example: Control: keep industries and airports away from homes, limit horns and loudspeakers.

items.name: Global warming
items.formula: The slow rise in Earth's temperature from the greenhouse effect.
items.example: Glaciers melt and sea level rises, as in the Himalayas and polar regions.

items.name: Greenhouse effect
items.formula: Carbon dioxide and other gases trap heat given off by the Earth.
items.example: Burning fossil fuels adds these gases.

items.name: Ozone depletion
items.formula: CFCs from air conditioners, fridges and sprays destroy stratospheric ozone.
items.example: The worst ozone hole is over Antarctica.

items.name: Acid rain
items.formula: Rain that picks up acids, such as sulphuric acid, from polluted air. It is called the "lake killer".
items.example: The "Black Triangle" over Poland, Czech Republic and south-east Germany is badly hit.

items.name: Saving biodiversity and the Earth
items.formula: Give rare species good living conditions.
items.example: Education, awareness and careful use of resources save the Earth.

mistakes.text: Global warming comes from the greenhouse effect; ozone depletion comes from CFCs. They are different problems.
Ecology is the study; the ecosystem is the community and its surroundings being studied.
Pollution has natural sources too, such as volcanoes and forest fires, but man-made ones are worse.
